subject: Workload snapshot + model recommendations — onboarding handoff
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@ingram-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Workload snapshot + model recommendations — onboarding handoff

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the kickoff today. Per our notes, I pulled together a short workload snapshot and an initial model-recommendation matrix to guide the onboarding sizing. Both files are attached.

Top-line summary from discovery:
- Primary workload: user-submitted long-form notes -> concise abstracts (summarization + light extraction).
- Typical input length (median): ~450 tokens; 95th percentile estimate: 1,200 tokens (see sheet).
- Expected concurrent active users at launch (month 1): 120; projected steady-state month 6 concurrency: 420.

Immediate asks for you to confirm:
1) Verify the 95th percentile request length — I put 1,200 tokens in the workbook as a conservative estimate.
2) Are examples in the sheet representative and free of regulated PHI/PII? If any rows contain sensitive fields, please flag them so we can advise on private deployment/KMS.
3) Target latency SLO for the user-facing endpoint — current internal target is 600ms p50 / 1.5s p95. Is that acceptable?

What we’ll deliver once you confirm the above: a 3-option model shortlist (low-latency small model, mid-tier accuracy/cost model, and a high-quality option for reserved capacity), a cost-throughput sketch for Hosted vs Dedicated, and a short playbook for warmup/caching and KV prefix usage.

Attachments: onboarding_workload_sheet.xlsx (xlsx), model_shortlist_matrix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — I’m looping in Monica and Vivek for sizing and kernel/quantization guidance.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@ingram-analytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@ingram-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 08:36:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Workload snapshot + model recommendations — onboarding handoff

Hi Priya — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 95th percentile number looks high compared to our internal analytics; our current telemetry shows 95th ~ 850 tokens for the summarization endpoint. The 1,200 figure could happen on some enterprise clients who paste long reports, but it's not the norm.
- Data class: most rows are standard business content (no PHI). There are a small number of client notes that reference customer identifiers — we can mark those rows for redaction.
- Latency SLO: 600ms p50 / 1.5s p95 is reasonable for the experience we want. For the MVP we can accept higher p95 if it materially reduces cost — would like to see the Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs.

Two quick asks: can you provide the QPS distribution over a 24h window (hourly) and an estimate for peak burst length (we see burst windows that last 20–30s occasionally)? I included a short screenshot of our traffic heatmap in the workbook comments.

Thanks — copying our engineering lead so they have visibility.

—Sara Liu
Product Ops Lead | Ingram Analytics
sara.liu@ingram-analytics.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@ingram-analytics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Workload snapshot + model recommendations — onboarding handoff

Thanks Sara — helpful context. Quick notes from an engineering/sizing perspective: 

- If 95th is 850 tokens (instead of 1,200) that materially reduces memory/KV cache footprint and allows us to consider a slightly larger context window model at lower cost. I’ll run two sizing scenarios (850 and 1,200) for p95 to show the delta.
- For bursts: we generally plan batching windows and elastic prewarmed slots. For 20–30s bursts we recommend having a small pool of warm workers with KV cache warmed via a short prefix-warm routine — I’ll include the warmup ops in the runbook.
- On data classification: if you mark/redact the rows that contain identifiers we can keep all other testing on Hosted. For any regulated rows we’ll recommend Private with KMS.

Action: I’ll produce two capacity sketches and a draft warmup/playbook by EOD Friday (Sep 3). Priya — can you share the HubSpot deal link and any procurement timeline?

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

I’m attaching our signed Data Sharing SOP (sop_data_sharing_form.pdf) per your ask. Also proposing two times for a technical sizing call next week:
- Tue, Sep 7, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed, Sep 8, 14:00–14:45 PT

Which works better for Redwood?

Thanks,
—Sara

Hi Sara — great, thanks for the updates and the SOP. Quick summary & next steps so we’re aligned before the sizing call tomorrow: 

Summary of confirmations:
- 95th percentile request length: 850 tokens (confirmed).
- Data: three flagged rows with identifiers — Redwood will exclude those from Hosted tests and we’ll recommend Private for any surrounding datasets that cannot be redacted.
- Latency SLO: 600ms p50 / 1.5s p95 target.
- Procurement target: PO by Sep 28; HubSpot deal HS-34912.

Deliverables for tomorrow’s 10:00 PT call (Tue, Sep 7):
1) Monica: two capacity sketches (p95 850 vs 1,200) showing GPU footprint, warm worker counts, and estimated unit cost for Hosted vs Dedicated.
2) Vivek: model shortlist rationale and preferred quantization/latency knobs for each option (we’ll present small-mid-large options and recommended default).
3) Priya: mutual action plan slide with procurement checklist and DocuSign link; I’ll also share the Drive folder during the call.
